feature: The timeline bar's Easing sets points and segments picked together
summary: Pick a segment on an open value graph, Shift-click a point, and the timeline bar's Easing names the curve they share or Mixed. A curve chosen there sets all of them in one undo step.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Add a title, animate its Scale and key it at three moments.
Click Graph in the Properties panel to open the Scale graph.
Click the second segment and choose Ease out in the timeline bar's Easing.
Click the first segment, then Shift-click the middle point. Easing reads Mixed.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Choose Ease out back in Easing. Both segments take it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command-Z once. Both segments go back.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Does a picked point taking the curve of the segment that leaves it match what you expect?
Is Mixed clear enough when the picked segments run on different curves?
With points picked alone, the bar still shows the key list (Ease In, Ease Out, Bezier). Is that switch noticeable, and does it bother you?
rough: The app goes further than the mock here: a picked last point, which starts no segment, sets the segment arriving at it, so a choice never skips a point.
Points alone still show Premiere's six eases in the bar and on their right-click, where the mock draws the ten curves everywhere: decision card on wherever-you-ease-a-key-a-segment-a-row-or-the-b.
Shift-clicking a point opens its value bar right over the line it is about to shape: filed as a-point-picked-on-an-open-graph-keeps-its-value.
